messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty ALERT — HIGH severity: sustained 5xx spike in az3. route=/v1/generate error_rate=8.3% window=60s. alert_id=PD-381922. auto-page oncall.

maria_oncall: Acked. I'm on it, pinging dashboards now.

pagerduty-bot: Incident PD-381922 acknowledged by maria_oncall. Escalation schedule frozen.

maria_oncall: Looks like the spike started ~12:33UTC, sudden jump in backend HTTP 502/503 from inference pods.

ben_sre: seeing same on metrics — tail latency fine but p50->p95 increased and 5xx ramped. Is this widespread or single pool?

ops-watch: Dashboard link: https://grafana.internal/r/az3/PD-381922 - error-rate, pod restarts, network errors. Most errors are 502 gateway timeouts from model-shard-proxy.

maria_oncall: quick check: k8s events show OOMKilled on model-shard-3c pod group around 12:31:50. Not massive evictions but several back-to-back.

ben_sre: running quick pod list:
```
kubectl -n serving get pods -l app=model-shard -o wide | grep az3
```
Seeing 3/10 pods RestartCount > 4.

claire_pm: Any immediate customer impact? We have a few customers on dedicated capacity in az3 — should we notify CS/Account teams?

maria_oncall: Need a scoping number. ops-watch can you run an queries count of failed requests by customer tier?

ops-watch: quick query: error_count_by_customer (last 5m): free-tier ~12% of failed requests, paid-tier ~5% (some retries). Total ~1.8k failed requests/minute. A handful of high-volume customers account for ~60% of fail rate.

maria_oncall: thanks. Plan: 1) enable cross-az fallback routing (divert a fraction to az2), 2) trigger autoscale for model-shard in az3, 3) if error rate doesn't drop in 3m, escalate to full fallback/divert.\
ben_sre: agree. I can flip the routing override. Preparing command now.\
maria_oncall: call out to on-call bridge: creating incident bridge now.\
incident-bot: Bridge created: https://bridges.internal/PD-381922 (maria_oncall, ben_sre, dan_platform)\
dan_platform: I'll watch infra scaling. If underlying nodes are constrained we may need to release capacity from burst pool.\
ben_sre: executing routing override (canary 20% diverted to az2):
```
curl -X POST https://internal-router/api/overrides \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"policy":"cross-az-divert","from":"az3","to":"az2","percent":20,"reason":"autoscale+5xx spike"}'
```
Response: 202 Accepted, override_id=ovr-20260315-01\
ops-watch: confirm: routed 20% outgoing traffic to az2. metrics updating.\
maria_oncall: monitoring error rate...\
ben_sre: initial effect: 5xx decreased to 6.1% within 45s on overall; az3-specific still around 9% but traffic reduction helps customer impact.\
claire_pm: Good — does that reduce errors for the big customers? Any visible improvement?\
ops-watch: high-volume customers show 30-40% fewer errors after canary divert. Paid-tier restore more quickly.\
dan_platform: autoscaler fired, +3 shards in az3 but they haven't stabilized yet; investigating OOM cause. Suspect a sudden input-length change causing memory blowouts on a subset of models.\
maria_oncall: any logs of unusually long sequences or batch size spikes?\
ben_sre: pulled recent request samples: a surge of long-context requests (~32k tokens) from a single customer integration on free-tier playground. That lines up with OOMs.\
claire_pm: contacting customer success to throttle that integration or ask customer to use streaming/limits? CC: @support-team\
maria_oncall: escalation: if error_rate stays >5% overall after 3m we'll increase divert to 60% and enable full fallback for affected routes. Agree?\
ben_sre: agree. Also enqueue a temporary rate-limit rule for the offending API key:
```
POST /internal/keys/limit
{ "key":"acct-9XJ...","qps":5 }
```
I'll apply after we confirm identity.\
ops-watch: PD reminder: automatic escalation in 5m if acked but not resolved.\
pagerduty-bot: Reminder: PD-381922 will auto-escalate at 12:40:36Z if unresolved.\
maria_oncall: applying targeted rate limit to the suspect key now.\
ben_sre: rate limit applied, verifying error rates...\
ops-watch: after rate limit + canary divert, overall 5xx now down to 3.2% in last 60s. High-volume customer errors down ~75%.\
maria_oncall: excellent. We can hold at 20% divert while autoscaler stabilizes + pods recover.\
claire_pm: Customer comms: I'll draft a brief note to affected accounts noting degraded performance and that we've mitigated; include ETA for full recovery ~30-60m. Want to wait until stabilized?\
ben_sre: leave the canary in place until all pods healthy and p95 latency back to baseline. Then slowly ramp divert back to 0%.\
dan_platform: nodes look healthy. OOM root cause: a regression in runtime memory accounting in release 1.12.3. Rolling back that subset to 1.12.2 on az3 now.\
maria_oncall: timeline: rollback started 12:38, expected finish 12:48.\
ops-watch: rollback progress: 60% pods on 1.12.2, rest restarting. Error rate trending down.\
ben_sre: once rollback done, I'll start a controlled rollback of the routing override: divert 20% -> 10% -> 0% in 2m steps, watch errors.\
maria_oncall: PD: marking progress in incident: partial mitigation achieved, customer impact reduced.\
pagerduty-bot: Note added to PD-381922: canary divert active, rate-limit applied to offending key, runtime rollback in progress.\
claire_pm: Sending comms now to top affected customers (short note + link to status page).\
maria_oncall: handing incident to ben_sre for watch while I take short break. Ben — can you own the rollback of traffic and final validation?\
ben_sre: taking over. Will ramp down divert when pods healthy.\
maria_oncall: thx — if you need escalation call Dan. I'm available on bridge. :thumbsup:\
ben_sre: rollback traffic plan executed: 20% -> 10% at 12:50 (ok) -> 0% at 12:52. No regression observed after final step. p95 and error-rate back to baseline.\
ops-watch: final metrics: error_rate=0.6% (normal), p95 latency within 10% of baseline. No additional OOMs after rollback.\
pagerduty-bot: PD-381922 resolved by ben_sre at 12:54:18Z.\
maria_oncall: good job team. Follow-ups: 1) postmortem to investigate why 1.12.3 memory regression slipped, 2) improve automatic detection for extremely long-context spikes and auto-throttle, 3) update runbook for canary divert thresholds.\
claire_pm: i'll own comms and postmortem coordination with SRE + product.\
ben_sre: filing incident runbook notes and linking replay logs.\
dan_platform: scheduling rollback patch to 1.12.2 for affected images and plan for a memory-accounting test in CI.\
maria_oncall: closing bridge. Great quick work. :party_parrot:
